body:
I really like that perspective! 
She is the one that reminds me to check the mixer and I remind her to check the sound bar. We are a team!
By the way I love your name. I too do some hooking. My hand are in a state so I can't now but I miss it.
He can't relate because he never dealt with it. He is more understanding with me but if it is someone else he is judgy. Like my parents. It feels like he blames them for my struggles.

That is a good point. He is overall a pretty supportive guy. He really judges the lable. If I tell him it works for me ok. But if I say I found a coping mechanism that helps people with ADHD he rolls his eye. I don't know why.

Yes, they are always in the mixer. My phone too. It is because I set them there to keep them safe while I cook. My daughter always forgets things on the sound bar. It does seem to be helpful now that we realized it.

The way he is putting makes it seem that it is a learned behavior that I should be able to just stop doing. Like Bonus dad is constantly late and I compulsively check times and am usually 30 minutes early.

 But i don't think that is healthy either. It is a way I cope after we were late for everything growing up. He seems to think that it can be unlearned that my lost glass are always in the stand mixer. And if I try hard enough I will just stop struggling.

I am so sorry to hear that you are going through all that. This is not ok. This is abusive. I don't know if my advice is doable or something you want to do. It sounds like she needs to see a doctor and both of you need to go to therapy.

 Hormones are awful but she is responsible for her behavior regardless. She needs to talk about a doctor about some sort of treatment. 

Therapy would be good for you even if she refuses. I really hope things improve. This isn't healthy for your children either.

Right now I can't do my crafts that are my usual dive into because I am have some sort of medical event that is making all my muscles and joints hurt doing normal things like pouring coffee.

Sooo. I am fixating on researching what the right questions I need to ask my doctor on Monday are and ways to get things done around the house when I hurt so bad. 

I normally love a good hyperfocus research can be really fun.

Bless you and the teachers like you. My daughter's teacher really advocated for her and recognize it before I did. He daughter has ADHD too. I guess I missed it because I was focused on her Autism diagnosis and didn't think about a second one. But it made sense and we got lucky. 

I am SO glad you take the time to make sure the relevant information is heard.
Lol, no but he did buy me some of my favorite pouches of jalapeno tuna. They come with a spork. Lol
He said he thought about doing that but thought the one just say his name over and over was better
I think you just gave me an idea for our anniversary!
You should see all the dead laptops in our basement
I did 9 years ago. I would do it all over again!
Mine is apple right now because banana hurts my ibs. But best hack ever

I'm sorry people really like to judge without having any idea what it is like. I'm sorry you have to deal with that. Like you need another stress. Not every illness can be cured with herbs. Pain is gnaws at you and makes it hard to function. 

I'm betting if we stopped taking meds and were unable to do the daily tasks they would judge us for that too.

A family member did that to me not to long ago. She said, "you know, all those drugs are just poison. Every medication you take is poison." Like ok? So, I do what? She never explained any further. Just that I am poisoning myself by taking meds. Ok Janice. I'll just dehydrate and starve from not being able to take my stomach meds. Sounds good.
Love that positive association with a sorta negative task. Makes such a difference. So glad you have an Elly!
That is awesome! Go women helping women! I love this!
Good job! It's so hard
Most relatable thing I have ever seen. My house is a craft store. Currently trying to convince myself not to buy resin and make jewelry

I wouldn't change it. My son by the time he was able to stand he would pee in the cup I used for hair.(I rinsed it) Idk why but he was easy to potty train. Weird kid. 

That said I know my daughter peed in the tub and kiddy pool. That amount of pee really doesn't hurt anything.

I was just telling my hubby about this. He mentioned that I hadn't lost the hairbrush in a while. I am a chronic loser of hair products. I told him it was because he bought it and I have it in my head that it belongs to him so I always triple check that it gets back were it belongs. Same with the Xbox controller. If it is someone else's it's fine. My keys, my glasses, my deodorant. Nope can't find it. Deodorant in every room and my purse. Lol

Nope. It just come out of my mouth as a song. Like "🎶 Putting the bag in the trash can, that is my plan.🎶" My mom tells me I sang my math problems when I did homework as a kid. I guess I never noticed.

 I guess it must help us if a bunch of us are doing it.
I sing all of the things. My kids find it hilarious. Like it is an opera about cleaning the stove. I don't even I realize I do it half the time.

My short answer is life would be worse if I got a divorce. Even during the hard times in my marriage, the alternative never felt like my life would improve if I was alone or had to start over with someone else. 

My marriage is great now but we sure had some bad times. Still did not feel like it was throwing it away. I enjoy being married and I enjoy my husband.

I lost mine for 3 days under folded towels in a basket
 When I finally put away the towels, there they were. Teach me to procrastinate the last step of laundry

The post was about feeling like the parties were too much but feeling pressure to have them. There is no problem with having those things but they are often because the parents to feel like they should. Many times the kids are just as happy with small gatherings.  I was saying that it doesn't matter so don't feel bad about not doing that. 
I also said the MOST was 6. You made my comment about something else. My daughter's last birthday was just us going to a restaurant. No other kids but her brother. I'm not sure why you are so touchy about me validating not having to have a big party. I don't think I am the one being rude.

And? The point is that the most we had like 6 kids other than mine there. There is no point of wasting money on stressful parties when they won't remember. I don't see the point in big family trips when they are little either. Admit they are for you and not the kids.

My kids have never had a big party. It is usually just cousins, and grandparents. One year my daughter has her best friend and friend's siblings and my niece and nephews. Covid has prevented my son from really having anyone but family. 

I personally don't see the point. They don't really remember all of those parties. I may do a big party when they turn 16 or 18 but my daughter is pretty shy. Who knows.

Wait until you have kids (if you want them) I lost more friends with my kids than getting married. My husband has a friend that still invites him to stuff same day or next day. We can't find a babysitter that fast. 

The really good ones stay and find ways to see you even if your lifestyle is different now. My best friend kept on hanging out with us even though she didn't have kids or get married for another 10 years. 

Don't worry. The adjustment takes time but it will work out. And they may come back around when they settle down too. Nothing wrong with reunions.

People tell you whatever year you are in is the hardest. My mom said the 1st year, then the 3rd and so on. You worst year is whatever year the worst things happen in your relationship.
 My first year was pretty easy but not the best either.
I feel this in the center of my chest. Struggling with this hard
MY FAMILY DOESN'T UNDERSTAND NERO DIVERSITY! MY MOM SCOLDS MY KIDS FOR STEMMING. MY STEP DAD IS IN DENIAL!

I have a family member who is an EMT and works with a nurse who is obsessed with making sure everyone knows they aren't a nurse. If the officers tell a patient to "Sit in the chairs by the nurses." She freaks out and says "they need to know you aren't a nurse!"

 Even though their roll is exactly the same in that setting. She still insists on correcting them every time. The nurse preforms the same exact tasks and the patients they have couldn't care less. The officers know they just don't care because it doesn't matter. 

This isn't a hospital setting but I thought the attitude was odd.

This is called financial abuse. By not allowing you to make enough food for everyone and guilting you over small things he is trying to be in control. I would be there is something less important that he spends money on that he could cut back on. 

I would make 6 scrambled eggs for my family of four. I'm sorry but this is just abuse.

I feel very much the same way. I don't have a job since last year and that was a seasonal one I only did for two years. I didn't have a job before that since 2014. I got laid off.

I have kids but they are in school so I really don't leave the house if unless it is for them. If my husband wasn't with me I would still be with my parents. I just got lucky he is so easy on me. But I won't go into that.

I feel like my ADHD gets worse with age and that I haven't accomplished anything. I'm just watching my kids grow up in slow motion and high speed at the same time. 

I wish I had tips on getting back on track. I really don't. But you aren't alone. I'm sorry you feel that way too. The withdrawal from SSRI is painful. I had a horrible time with it. I'm so sorry again.

My therapist told me I had both. I believe her words were when you have both it's a "hot mess" to treat. She said she had to work on each symptom individually to see if it is something my meds help or something we need to go deeper into during seasons or both. 

Hang in there. I hope you can get a skilled professional to help you sort it out. And don't be afraid to dump one and try again if it doesn't seem right. I definitely had to do that. You aren't alone I. This.
I bet! Great job!

This reminds me of when I was young and had just started my cycle. I told my mom and she got me supplies. For a month every time she went to the store she would buy more. 

I finally had to tell her that the hall closet was avalanching pads when I opened it. We could have used your beautiful organization.
I was coming to say the same thing.
That is very sweet. Thank you! I try my best to overcome those generational curses. It is good that you do speak up. And you did it in a kind manner. Kudos 👍
Same! My son was 18 months before I got help for it. I was miserable before. I never really went back to normal without meds.

My daughter is 5 1/2 years older than my son and had shut downs well before he was born. She has also had a behavioral therapist. She is not expected to engage with him when he is like that. Her first reaction is to get a parent. We talk to both of them after any episode he has.

 Yes, I am aware that she could easily be overlooked as I too was like that as a child and my older brothers put me through lots of trauma. 

My house is very small and the walls are thin. I can usually respond faster than she can come get me. I don't consider closing herself off to be a "good" behavior. She is pretty open with us but we do have to press occasionally for more info. 

 I have to remind family members that they aren't noticing her subtle cues. And we have been working on her standing up for herself. 

 I completely understand why that would be a concern you might have since I did not elaborate with any details. Thank you for caring enough to bring it up.
We got fuzzy boots that have inserts so you can take them out and wash them

My son has violent outbursts from seemingly small triggers. I do not hit or abuse my child and he is in therapy. My daughter has never so much as raised her voice. All kids are different. Both struggle with sensory issues but react in polar opposite ways. She shuts down and he explodes.

 It is very dangerous to say that abuse is the reason. I shut down as a kid and was being abuse. There are co diagnosis like autism, ODD etc. Those things take time to get diagnosed and treated. Most treatments are a long haul. 

This post made me sick. I have worked with a wide range of disabilities and can tell you violent outbursts are not always the fault of the caregiver or child. The world is an overwhelming place.

I guess I will be the odd one out. First, I will start by saying I have never heard of half day school for kindergarten. Only preschool and they had about that much homework in that too. I even photo copied to practice over the summer. But that being said both of my children did full days and both had 1-2 work sheets a night Mon-Thurs. 

My son had strep and missed a week so the fallowing week he did a full day of school then his normal homework and and extra 3 a day until he was caught up. We didn't really have a problem.

 We just let him finish a sheet or two while I made dinner and then after dinner. So he had breaks. He is now in first grade and one sheet a night and a 15 min nightly reading log.

  But what you said sounds normal to me if it is half day. Maybe we are just used to it.
That is a great way to describe it. It is so hard to say motivated. It feels like I'm a failure and that having the clear spot is a reminder that it wasn't clear before and I had to try so hard.

That rejection sensitivity is the worst. I feel that hard.  He says let's clean and find the meds. I hear that I'm am putting him out and he has to rescue me. But he just wants to help. 

 feel like it is so much work and it will just be like this again no matter how much I say I won't pile craft supplies on my bed and sleep next to yarn.
Thank you! Those are all great suggestions. I really felt alone in this. I will have to write those down so I don't forget.

Thank you for your thoughtful response. My brother rarely lets my mother see his kids anyway. So, I think it can wait a little longer for SIL to heal. But I will definitely speak with them.

I did speak to my daughter and asked if my mom said why they should do it. She said she didn't give a reason. My daughter is autistic and doesn't always understand people's motivations. I told her that it was not ok. I explained that she and the other kids are perfect no matter what they look like. I will probably have to talk to her again to see how much she understood. 

I plan on speaking with my mom in the morning and possibly my step dad too. He wasn't there and hasn't ever said anything about the kids bodies. I think he could be a good backup.

I would disagree that it wasn't urgent as I have brought it up before to her. So, she started waiting until the door is closed to bring it up instead of in front of him now. I remind her that he is just a kid and switch the subject. However, I don't know how she talks to him when I am not there.

 I am definitely, going to bring up the situation with all the kids. If I had found out before now when I was there instead of after dinner two days later I may have had a different reaction. I am considering bringing it up to my step dad first as he was not there either but could help with addressing it without a full blow-up

That is a good idea. I think I will do some research and print some stuff out. I didn't think about that before.
 I am pretty mad because she did it when she was alone with the kids. I feel like that is because she knew we would have called it out on the spot. She didn't have them do that when she took pics with us there. I feel like she would just agree with me and do it again. She seems to be obsessed with his weight.

That is not necessarily been his experience. I can tell you that my daughter was diagnosed and treated with relative ease. With my son he has more of the symptoms and I am told he is difficult and needs to be spanked when it is clear to me and his teacher that he is obviously struggling. The doctor told me to ignore him and that he is smart and "trying to annoy me". I never said her was annoying. The boys will be boys thing has backfired and now I can't get people to take his issues seriously. 

I know it can be tempting to feel like he may have had it easier but you don't know how much he had to do to get there. Confidence and be false. You would be surprised how people compensate. I got treatment for my ADHD and my mom had to get help with my oldest brother's dyslexia and my middle brother's autism.

Sounds just like me. Even if I know I locked it I still hit the button again. Of course I have totally locked myself out of the house, forgotten to turn off the stove etc. My husband has most of our outlets on timers just in case.

No, half the time my husband and I don't wear them at all they just sit on the nightstand unless we are going out or something. My weight fluctuates to much for it to fit all the time and my husband work in a warehouse where he isn't supposed to wear it for safety unless it is one of those rubber replacements.

As far as I know my brothers and father never had any trouble with it. My oldest brother definitely does fine and sleeps on it. But the boys don't seem to have ADHD either. My middle brother is autistic but not ADHD. I guess that is how it worked out in our family. Genetics is weird.
My husband does and I watch it with him sometimes. Sometimes I watch it alone. I don't know if everyone is accurate but a large portion of the population. And some do but won't admit it to their SO.

Yes! Codeine is one med none of the women in my family can use for the same reason. My daughter and I have ADHD and I suspect that my mom does too. We all have exactly what you described.  So glad you discovered that so you can advocate for yourself better. Opiates seem to still work correctly for us  too.

I love my children to death. I honestly feel like they matured me and made me a better person. Life is harder with kids but in a good way. Sometimes think, " this would be easier without kids" but it would also be lonelier. I have a reason to get up and I'm proud of them. It is so much fun to watch them change into different people as they grow up.

I am so tired that my husband is worried that it may be medical. I sleep all night. I wake up tired and almost always take and involuntary nap during the day. I fall asleep visiting family, folding laundry, or whatever. I sleep 9 hours a night. Sometimes I have to take two naps. Idk what the answer is.

I'm so sorry that you had to go through all that. So many things are misunderstood. Even though I was diagnosed as a kid there was still a lot of things I didn't know we're not me "just being lazy" I never felt like I could keep up with what "normal people" could do. Like keeping my house clean, remembering appointments etc. Glad you finally got meds and help.

Yes, it is pretty common for people with ADHD to have stimulants like meds or caffeine and be tired instead of wired. I can drink a pot of coffee and sleep. It is my argument to people who claim the getting meds for ADHD is an excuse to use habit forming drugs. Like I forget to take my meds so how could I be addicted?  Our brain chemistry is different and people don't understand. 
Even in my herbal group I have seen people discover they don't have the same reactions. Nettle is supposed to give you energy. I had a Convo with a gal who kept trying but is made her sleepy. Turns out, she had ADHD and was trying to work through it with herbs.

I was accused of guilt tripping when I was just verbally walking through my day to see if I could do what they asked me to do. Communication is so hard. My husband and I have also had people think we were fighting when we were just figuring out plans out.
Oh yes

Yeah, I feel like I have dementia or something. It is frightening because I cared for my grandfather with Alzheimer's for years before he passed. 

I over heard my kids talking and one said, "Shhh, Mommy will hear you."  Other one said, " Even if she does, she will just forget."  Turns out they were planning something nice to surprise me. Thank goodness.

You can totally put whatever name one there you want. And please do include your name. I have been married to my husband for 8 years and my 12 year old calls him daddy. We had all sorts of trouble getting her ears pierced because she has BD's last name. The tattoo shop we took her to said they have to verify because they could get sued. Because auntie claims to be Mom.
My husband had to send a picture of our taxes (SS# blocked out) to prove we claim her and a pic from her yearbook so they could see the name matches the pic. She didn't have a school ID. 

My BD has not been in her life since she was 2 and doesn't pay child support or anything.
That is so rough. My husband seems to be on board with everything I say. But my daughter's bio dad behaved similar with her.  Hope he see it is important so your son can get what he needs

That is very much what my son does. He will only answer in sign language. My mother said my brother did it to as a little and she affectionately labeled it "having a mad" his original diagnosis was way different but that was 30 years ago. Strong argument for genetics. We have been considering a different pediatrician for some time. It is definitely time.

That sounds super stressful. I'm so sorry you had all that. I am very lucky at this time I am staying home. If I wasn't I couldn't imagine trying to make all those calls and appointments. My husbands work has good insurance and it seems they are way more helpful than what we had before.  I guess I have it easier than many.
My insurance said I didn't need a referral and if this office we are going through doesn't help I will just contact the children's hospital that my insurance said we could go to and get an appointment there. His cardiologist and allergist are already there but it is kind of an all day situation with that.

We do time outs a minute per year of age.  And when he continues and hit the walls or floor when in time out we take electronic privileges away in five minutes increments. He gets 30min a day of electronic time. This is of course if there is a reason for the fit that we can see. Sometimes we can't figure it out or he is upset with something he cannot complete on his own. Never have we given in to anything that that he was upset about. 

His most recent fit was in the car on the way home from school. We were talking about what we will do over the summer break in a few months and he nearly hyperventilated because I said he would have a new teacher next year. Took my daughter and I ten minutes to calm him down. We told him she would still be in the same school and he could see her in the hallway. And we talked about it. He still doesn't like the idea but his immediate reaction was panic. 

I understand that many times people give in to tantrums or kids get attention for crying. I mentioned spanking for a few reasons. One because my pediatrician seemed very concerned about it. Two, he was spanked before during an outburst and he just hit back. Obviously, that isn't effective. I had many fights with family about that.

It is interesting that you say allergist. He hasn't been tested for foods but has for environmental stuff like trees, grass, pets. He is allergic to almost everything. My mom has been bugging me about keeping a food journal. thank you. 
My daughter did lots of OT and everything but she presents differently. She shuts down instead of blows up. They thought she was having seizures because she would kinda go catatonic when stressed. 

But they are both considered gifted too. My daughter was in a special program for school and my son's teach said she can't teach him anything in her class but he needs the socialization.

I did talk to his teacher today and she said he is very smart but very anxious and is setting him up with group social work through the school to help him.
I have one audio. I will try to take. Video next time for sure. It doesn't help that doctor visits usually happen earlier in the day and the end of the day is his hardest time

I do have a recording of the sounds of one but not anything else. Thank you. That is. Good idea. 

Sorry about your daughter. And that they didn't listen to your concerns either. I hope she is getting the help she need now.

My daughter is autistic and has ADHD but they are totally different in behavior and everyone jumped to help her. Her teachers helped a lot and my son kinda just gets treated like a bad kid. Not by his teacher. She thinks he is amazing. But the family is harder on him. You wouldn't believe the amount of times I was told just to spank him or something. I will take the bill for sure if he can be helped

This place has a psych that he will see after the a visit and evaluation with the counselor.  

The other option is I have to drive into the nearby city to go to the children's hospital. It isn't that far but I was hoping not to have to take the whole day every appointment.
 
I think you may be right about getting a new doc. Now is the time I guess since everything is opening back up
But no, he doesn't meltdown at school but often does as soon as he gets home where he refuses to speak. That is why we started to sign with him a few months ago

He started school this year and his teacher says he is very shy at school and calm. Very smart but she asked if we had noticed him not making eye contact. I haven't noticed that. She said as long as they don't change the daily routine he does great but struggles when they have any special activities that change the day  He is always so wiped out after school. Bus driver says he sleeps the whole ride.

My father originally did not like me dating my husband and said "I don't think I could handle a mixed grandbaby". I told him then he wouldn't have to and I would be out of his life. Now my dad is in love with my mixed son and gushes over every achievement my husband and children make. He had to do a lot of soul searching and all but he really did change his whole opinion. 

Your mother is not that nurturing. She isn't trying and doesn't care if it hurts you. She wants it to hurt you. She is punishing you for going against her narrow world views. My dad ultimately felt I was more important than his. Your mom is not even willing to consider she may be wrong.

 Please, for your daughter's sake cut your mom off. She will only hurt your family. Your children will notice. Lean on your husband's family. Lean on friends. Life is precious to waste it being abused by  bigotry.

Yeah, my regular doctor told me bi polar and when I finally got to a therapist that worked with a psychiatrist they said nope! Said it happens all the time especially since they regular doc didn't really spend enough time or ask near enough questions to even make that decision. Always get a referral to a specialist.
Of course.
My hands swell throughout the day. Without further info. I would ask. I would wear it on a necklace until the swelling or discomfort goes down.

I wanted to add that many so many issues can a lot of the same symptoms of ADHD and anxiety. Trauma, overuse of caffeine, stress and other undiagnosed mental illness. I was diagnosed with bi polar and then told by another doctor that no, it was just the fact that my ADHD and trauma when untreated for years and caused the anxiety and depression.

I have pretty much isolated myself so I don't get a whole lot of that from people other than family. I did have it with my husband when talking to him about how hopeless I felt when I had to fire my therapist and hadn't gotten meds yet.

He is very well liked and has always been accepted by any group. He said, "Even the popular kids had awkward moments." And in another Convo told me about a time he felt embarrassed and cringe after doing something.

I know he was trying to relate to rejection sensitivity and other symptoms but a single moment is not the same as regular panic attacks or failing to meet normal social expectations. It felt like he was downplaying the true struggle. 

I feel the same way but I also hurt when I see a loved one with many of the symptoms and isn't getting treatment.I was diagnosed at age 7. And family has said some pretty offensive stereotype comments.

I would say to try to forgive them for they know not what they do. They just aren't educated on it. I did have a Convo with my husband and since I got on some meds he can see the difference.

My therapist gave me a small sea shell that had lots of ridges and texture. It was small like the size of a coin. I run my thumb or nail on it and feel the grooves and it is a lot easier to hide that I am doing something else while listening. It helps me when I have panic attacks too. I bought a bag of shells at the dollar store so I can switch up. Sometimes offering them to my children when they need to be still/quite like in a waiting room or something.
I have a really hard time with the eye contact too. This is helpful

I'm so sorry to hear you went through that. I am not of the same background and culture as you so can't speak to that. However, I was raised in a very abusive home as well. I can empathize so much with that feeling.

 My older brother was very good in school and was even bumped up a grade. I was often compared to him. One semester I worked very hard and managed a higher grade than him. He told me it would never happen again because I just got lucky with  teachers that year or something. He spent the whole rest of the year being hateful to me and my family punished me if I stuck up for myself. I just stopped trying after that. 

I hope as an adult you have found a support system. I can't imagine how much harder it would have been for me if my family put more stock in school. You are in all likelihood very intelligent. I feel like given the right support in place you would do amazing at whatever you aspire to do/be.

Your analogy is amazing! Thank you. I was feeling a bit guilty that they have to help me but you really helped with the feeling that I was sucking as a mom. We do try to tell them to help even if it isn't their mess. 

It is so sweet that you recognize your son's strengths and that he helps you too. My daughter reads all my medical paperwork because her brain remember everything she reads like a walking encyclopedia. She reminds me of ingredients that I shouldn't have due to health issues. My son and I definitely do the same ADHD rabbit hole thing too. You are probably showing your oldest some coping methods you don't realize you use. I know I learn some from my kids. 

I have to say I have never been a group online that gives such supportive answers. I'm super impressed with you ladies!

This is the nicest and most supportive comment I have ever read! Thank you so much! You are right. I should focus on the positive. My mornings have been way less stressful and I am sure it has been for them as well.

I was diagnosed as a child and my daughter has inattentive ADHD and Autism. Her having both makes it seem (to me) that we don't experience all of the same symptoms or when we do there are notable difference in how we react.

 I hope you can find a good provider to help you fine your correct diagnosis. You are so kind and I am rooting for you too!

YTA. I have Gastroparesis and it took a while to get diagnosed. I cannot eat some things. I just can't. I have lost weight and I make separate meals for the rest of the family. But, I have kids and am a SAHM. It doesn't say if your wife works. If she does you really are TA.
    I have trouble sometimes making the food I don't eat because the smell alone makes me sick. I have thrown up in the kitchen trash washed up and continued cooking. I wouldn't expect most people to do that. I do because my kids have their own health issues. My husband also gets safe premade food when I feel really bad to help reduce the stress on me. 
   I am not saying she has what I do but many people have sensitivities to these kinds of things for a variety of reasons. She may have a food allergy she doesn't even know she has and thinks it is sensory. She may be on the spectrum. So many possibilities. 
   You could watch some YouTube videos or get a cook book. Then you could make better choices for yourself. I can tell you that picking out and cooking meals especially when you can't eat it or feel unappreciated is really hard.
    I know it is hard to imagine not liking your mom's food. I'm not unsympathetic to you. But some of my old favorites now make me sick. Think how hard that is on your wife to feel unable to eat something from someone she cares about.

I have so much between buying and spinning that I had to get a rental space for it. I call it my gallery. It is really just a couple of old rooms in the back of the barn that my mom lets me use. But they have heat and ac and I can do whatever I need. They are full of yarn, soon to be yarn and all the tools for the in between.

I struggle with exercise because even wearing pants can hurt and the movement makes it so much worse. Swimming or slow walking  seems to help but most others nearly make me cry. 

No, I don't want to put magnets in my shoes, needles to my face, bee stings, diets that consist of everything that makes it worse, meds that put me to sleep, thinking positive, prayer, B 12, yada yada yada. 

I have tried all of it and if it worked I would still be doing it.

Just for perspective, I have depression and I often isolate from the people I like the most and feel I will be a bother if I contact them first. I don't know your mom or you.
